[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This guidance defines what goes in an Azure DevOps (ADO) User Story — the required fields, the content format for each field, the tagging conventions, and the relationship links that connect the story to the artifacts upstream (Epics, Features) and downstream (GitHub Issues, PRs, deployed code). It serves as the single reference for anyone creating a User Story in ADO, whether the story carries BDD Gherkin acceptance criteria or traditional prose criteria.
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#who-this-is-for]

### Who This Is For

**Primary:** Product owners, business analysts, and program managers who create User Stories in Azure DevOps.

**Secondary:** Engineers who consume User Stories during sprint planning and need to understand the expected structure. Engineering leads who review stories before sprint commitment.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#the-problem-this-solves]

### The Problem This Solves

User Stories in ADO are the primary unit of sprint planning. Every story eventually flows downstream — into engineer task decomposition, agent specs, pull requests, and deployed code. When stories are inconsistently structured, three problems emerge:

1. **Sprint planning friction** — engineers spend meeting time asking clarifying questions about stories that should have been self-explanatory
2. **Traceability gaps** — without consistent tagging and linking, the chain from business requirement to deployed code breaks, creating compliance risk in regulated environments
3. **Handoff ambiguity** — engineers interpret loosely-written acceptance criteria differently, producing implementations that are technically complete but behaviorally wrong

A standard story format eliminates these problems by making every story self-contained, unambiguous, and traceable.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#part-1-user-story-structure]

## Part 1: User Story Structure

Every ADO User Story has four content sections: Title, Story Narrative, Acceptance Criteria, and Tags. This structure applies regardless of whether the story uses BDD or prose acceptance criteria.

> **Mapping a BDD capability to the Boards hierarchy:** when stories are generated from `.feature` files via `/eap-decom-spec-export-boards`, a single `.feature` capability maps to an ADO **Feature**, and each implementation **layer or screen** of that capability becomes a child **User Story** — paired 1:1 with the GitHub issue that executes it (backend `[layer]` chain, one per UI screen, testing, infrastructure). This is finer-grained than the legacy "one story per `.feature`" model: it lets each layer be sized, sprinted, assigned, and tracked independently, and lets the parent Feature roll up its state natively from its child Stories. The four content sections below apply to each individual User Story; see Part 4 for how a capability decomposes and Part 5 for the hierarchy and 1:1 mapping.
page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#title]

### Title

**Format:** `[Concern] — [Capability summary]`

The title has two parts separated by an em dash:
- **Concern** — the functional area or bounded context (matches the concern directory name in `docs/requirements/functional/`)
- **Capability summary** — a short phrase describing what the system does (verb-oriented, not noun-oriented)

**Examples:**

| Good | Why |
|------|-----|
| Enrollment — Submission validation | Clear concern, clear capability, verb-oriented |
| Eligibility — Real-time determination | Specific functional area, specific action |
| Clock — Timezone-aware time conversion | Matches the concern directory name exactly |
| Notification — Email delivery retry | Describes what the system does, not what it is |

| Bad | Why |
|-----|-----|
| Enrollment feature | No concern/capability separation, too vague |
| Implement validation service | Implementation-oriented, not behavior-oriented |
| Bug fix for member lookup | Not a user story — this is a bug work item type |
| Sprint 14 work | Describes a container, not a deliverable |

**Rules:**
- Use the exact concern name from the project's domain model or glossary — do not abbreviate or create synonyms
- Keep the capability summary under 10 words
- Do not include sprint numbers, assignee names, or priority indicators in the title
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#story-narrative]

### Story Narrative

**Format:** As a / I need / So that

```
As a [role]
I need [capability — what the system does for this role]
So that [business value — why this capability matters]
```

**Rules:**

| Element | Guidance |
|---------|----------|
| **Role** | Use a role as the system sees it — "eligibility worker," "member," "claims adjudicator," not a job title like "senior analyst" or a team name like "enrollment team" |
| **Capability** | Describe the system behavior from the role's perspective — "my enrollment submission validated immediately" not "the validation service to process enrollments" |
| **Business value** | State the outcome in business terms — "I receive clear feedback on errors before processing" not "the system returns a 400 response" |

The story narrative establishes the business context. It answers: who benefits, what they need, and why it matters. It does not describe implementation details.

**Using AI for this step:**

> "I have a `.feature` file for [concern] — [capability]. Generate the story narrative in As a / I need / So that format. The primary user role is [role]. The business value is [plain language outcome]."
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#acceptance-criteria]

### Acceptance Criteria

The acceptance criteria define what "done" means. The format depends on the story type.
page_texts.14:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#for-bdd-stories-the-default-for-behavioral-requirements]

#### For BDD Stories (the default for behavioral requirements)

The acceptance criteria **are** the Gherkin scenarios — verbatim, not summarized.

```
Acceptance Criteria:

@FR-ENR-SUB-010
Scenario: Complete enrollment submission is accepted
  Given a member submits an enrollment with all required fields
  When the submission is validated
  Then the validation result is "accepted"

@FR-ENR-SUB-020
Scenario: Missing email address is rejected
  Given a member submits an enrollment without an email address
  When the submission is validated
  Then the validation result is "rejected"
  And the error code is "EMAIL_REQUIRED"
```

**Critical rule:** Paste the full Given/When/Then text from the `.feature` file. Do not summarize scenarios into bullet points. Do not paraphrase. The acceptance criteria field must contain the same text that will become the automated test. If the engineer needs to "interpret" the acceptance criteria, they are written wrong.
page_texts.15:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#for-non-bdd-stories]

#### For Non-BDD Stories

Use a numbered checklist with independently verifiable items:

```
Acceptance Criteria:

1. [ ] Terraform module provisions an S3 bucket with versioning enabled and AES-256 encryption
2. [ ] Bucket policy restricts access to the application IAM role only
3. [ ] terraform plan shows no changes after a second apply (idempotent)
4. [ ] Module passes terraform validate and tflint with zero errors
```

**Rules for non-BDD criteria:**
- Each item must be independently verifiable — an observer can confirm pass/fail without subjective judgment
- Use concrete values — "AES-256 encryption" not "appropriate encryption"
- Avoid "should" or "properly" — state the exact expected outcome
page_texts.16:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#tags]

### Tags

Tags provide metadata for filtering, reporting, and traceability. Apply them as ADO tags on the work item.

**Required tags:**

| Tag | Format | Purpose |
|-----|--------|---------|
| `concern:<name>` | `concern:enrollment` | Links the story to its functional area. Must match the concern directory name in `docs/requirements/functional/`. |
| `bdd` | `bdd` | Present only on stories with Gherkin acceptance criteria. Signals that the AC field contains executable scenarios. |

**Conditional tags:**

| Tag | Format | When to Apply |
|-----|--------|---------------|
| `sprint:<N>` | `sprint:14` | When the story is committed to a specific sprint |
| `blocked` | `blocked` | When the story has an unresolved dependency |
| `spike` | `spike` | When the story is a research/investigation task, not a deliverable |

**Do not use tags for:**
- Priority — use the ADO Priority field
- Assignee — use the ADO Assigned To field
- Status — use the ADO State field (New, Active, Resolved, Closed)

page_texts.18:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#required-fields]

### Required Fields

These fields must be populated when the story is created.

| ADO Field | Content Source | Example |
|-----------|---------------|---------|
| **Title** | `[Concern] — [Capability summary]` | Enrollment — Submission validation |
| **Work Item Type** | Always `User Story` | User Story |
| **State** | `New` at creation | New |
| **Description** | The Story Narrative (As a / I need / So that) | As a member, I need my enrollment submission validated immediately, so that I receive clear feedback on any errors before the submission is processed |
| **Acceptance Criteria** | BDD: Verbatim Gherkin scenarios. Non-BDD: Numbered checklist. | See [Acceptance Criteria](#acceptance-criteria) |
| **Tags** | `concern:<name>`, plus `bdd` if applicable | `concern:enrollment, bdd` |
| **Area Path** | The team's area path per ADO project configuration | `EAP\Enrollment` |
| **Iteration Path** | The sprint iteration when committed, or the backlog path when uncommitted | `EAP\Sprint 14` or `EAP\Backlog` |
page_texts.19:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#optional-fields]

### Optional Fields

These fields are populated during refinement or sprint planning, not at story creation time.

| ADO Field | When to Populate | Guidance |
|-----------|-----------------|----------|
| **Story Points** | At refinement or sprint planning | Use the [sizing guidelines](#sizing-by-scenario-count) — scenario count provides a starting estimate, engineers adjust for implementation complexity |
| **Priority** | At backlog grooming | 1 = Must have this sprint, 2 = Should have, 3 = Could have, 4 = Won't have this sprint |
| **Assigned To** | At sprint planning | The engineer who will decompose and own the story |
| **Discussion** | Ongoing | Use for refinement questions, scope clarifications, and decision records. Do not put acceptance criteria in Discussion. |

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#bdd-stories-behavioral]

### BDD Stories (Behavioral)

Use BDD stories when the requirement describes **what the system does in response to inputs** — observable behavior with verifiable outcomes. This applies to both **functional requirements** (tagged `@FR-`) and **behavioral non-functional requirements** (tagged `@NFR-`) — quality attributes that are testable at the unit/integration level with deterministic inputs and outputs.

**Indicators that a story should be BDD:**
- The requirement can be expressed as "Given [context], When [action], Then [outcome]"
- The requirement has clear inputs and expected outputs
- The requirement involves business rules, validation, or domain logic
- Multiple edge cases or error paths exist
- The non-functional attribute is testable per-request or per-operation (not system-wide load/chaos)

**Examples of BDD-appropriate requirements:**
- Enrollment submission validation (`@FR-`)
- Eligibility determination rules (`@FR-`)
- Claims adjudication logic (`@FR-`)
- Notification routing rules (`@FR-`)
- Cache expiration behavior (`@FR-`)
- Circuit breaker thresholds (`@NFR-`)
- Session timeout enforcement (`@NFR-`)
- Input sanitization rules (`@NFR-`)
- Rate limit per-request enforcement (`@NFR-`)
- Retry backoff behavior (`@NFR-`)
page_texts.22:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#non-bdd-stories]

### Non-BDD Stories

Use non-BDD stories when the requirement does not describe behavioral input/output logic. This includes **systemic non-functional requirements** — quality attributes that require load testing, chaos engineering, or infrastructure-level measurement and cannot be verified by a deterministic unit/integration test.

**Categories of non-BDD stories:**

| Category | Examples | AC Format |
|----------|----------|-----------|
| **Infrastructure** | Provision S3 bucket, configure EKS cluster, set up monitoring | Numbered checklist with concrete resource specs |
| **Systemic non-functional requirements** | P95 latency < 200ms, 99.9% availability, backup RPO < 1 hour | Numbered checklist with measurable thresholds |
| **UI/UX layout** | Dashboard displays three columns, navigation bar includes logout button | Numbered checklist with visual specifications or mockup references |
| **Documentation** | Write API reference, update runbook, create architecture diagram | Numbered checklist with deliverable descriptions |
| **Spike/Research** | Evaluate three caching strategies, prototype SSO integration | Numbered checklist with deliverable artifacts (decision doc, prototype, comparison matrix) |

> **Behavioral vs. Systemic NFRs:** If a non-functional requirement can be expressed as "Given [context], When [action], Then [deterministic outcome]" and tested at the unit/integration level, it is a behavioral NFR — use a BDD story with `@NFR-` tagged scenarios. If it requires system-wide load testing, chaos injection, or infrastructure measurement, it is a systemic NFR — use a non-BDD story with a numbered checklist. See `spec-nfr-create` for the classification decision tree.

page_texts.24:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#sizing-by-scenario-count]

### Sizing by Scenario Count

For BDD stories, the number of Gherkin scenarios provides a starting estimate for story points. The engineer adjusts based on implementation complexity during sprint planning.

| Scenario Count | Typical Range | Rationale |
|----------------|---------------|-----------|
| 3–5 scenarios | 2–3 points | Small, focused capability — one concern, few edge cases |
| 6–10 scenarios | 3–5 points | Medium capability — multiple paths, some complexity |
| 11–15 scenarios | 5–8 points | Large capability — significant business logic, many edge cases |

For non-BDD stories, use the acceptance criteria checklist count as a rough proxy, adjusted for technical complexity.
page_texts.25:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#how-a-capability-decomposes-into-stories]

### How a capability decomposes into Stories

When stories come from `/eap-decom-spec-export-boards`, the decomposition is **by layer**, not by sub-capability. One `.feature` → one **Feature**; each layer/screen → one child **User Story** (1:1 with its GitHub issue):

| Layer | Becomes a Story | Sizing basis |
|-------|-----------------|--------------|
| Backend implementation | `[data]` / `[service]` / `[bff]` Stories when the backend spine is deep enough to warrant a `[layer]` chain; otherwise one implementation Story | functional scenario count |
| UI (Presentation) | **one Story per screen** in the UI Contract | that screen's `@FR-*-UI-*` scenario count |
| Testing | one Story per implementation/UI Story it verifies | mirrors the thing it tests |
| Infrastructure | one Story when `scope=infra` constraints exist | provisioning scope |

This keeps each Story independently demonstrable while the **Feature** aggregates the whole capability.
page_texts.26:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#when-to-split-further]

### When to split further

Within a single layer's Story, split when any of these signals appear:

| Signal | Action |
|--------|--------|
| More than 15 functional Gherkin scenarios in one feature | Split the `.feature` by sub-capability — each becomes its own Feature with its own Story set |
| More than 12 UI scenarios for one screen | The "screen" is really two screens — split it; each gets its own UI Story and UI Contract |
| Scenarios span multiple concerns | One Feature per concern — do not mix `enrollment` and `eligibility` scenarios |
| Estimated at more than 8 story points | Decompose into smaller, independently demonstrable Stories |
| Contains both behavioral and infrastructure work | Already separated by the layer model (behavioral vs. `agent:infrastructure` Story) |

**The splitting rule:** Each Story should be independently demonstrable at sprint review. A UI Story splits **by screen** — never separate a screen's UI scenarios from the functional behavior they render. If you cannot demo a Story without first demonstrating another, they may need to be reordered (via prerequisite tiers) but they remain separate Stories.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#upstream-links-epics-and-features]

### Upstream Links (Epics and Features)

Every User Story links to a parent in the ADO hierarchy:

```
Epic → Feature → User Story
```

| Link Type | Guidance |
|-----------|----------|
| **Epic** | A major business initiative or program-level objective. One Epic contains many Features. |
| **Feature** | A business capability — maps 1:1 to a `.feature` file. One Feature contains one child User Story per implementation layer/screen of that capability. Its state **rolls up** from its child Stories. |
| **User Story** | One layer or screen of the capability (backend `[data]`/`[service]`/`[bff]`, a UI screen, testing, or infrastructure) — small enough for one sprint, paired 1:1 with the GitHub issue that executes it. |

When `/eap-decom-spec-export-boards` runs, it creates the **Feature** first (the PO planning gate), then a child **User Story** per layer/screen as the engineer exports GitHub issues. Always set each Story's **Parent** link to its Feature — orphan stories break the rollup and traceability.
page_texts.29:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#downstream-links-github-issues-and-prs]

### Downstream Links (GitHub Issues and PRs)

Each child **User Story** is paired **1:1** with exactly one GitHub Issue (the layer/screen it represents). The GitHub Issue's `## Enterprise Work Item` section references the parent **Feature**'s `WI#`/`AB#`; the Story↔Issue pairing is recorded when `/eap-decom-spec-export-boards --stories` creates the Story.

The downstream traceability chain (per layer):

```
ADO Feature (WI#4800)  — the capability; state rolls up from its Stories
  ├─ ADO User Story (WI#4821, layer: service)  ── 1:1 ──  GitHub Issue #42
  │      └─ Agent PR #43 → merged commit
  └─ ADO User Story (WI#4822, layer: ui:compare) ── 1:1 ── GitHub Issue #55
         └─ Agent PR #56 → merged commit
```

`/eap-decom-spec-sync-exports` keeps each Story's state mirrored to its 1:1 issue and the Feature rolled up; `/eap-decom-spec-sync-exports --audit` validates that every issue has exactly one Story and no orphans exist. You do not hand-manage GitHub Issues or PRs — the engineer and the sync command do. Your responsibility is a well-formed Feature with correctly-parented Stories so the rollup and 1:1 mapping hold.
page_texts.30:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#cross-reference-format]

### Cross-Reference Format

Per [STD-GOV-AI-003](../../../../standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md), the enterprise work item cross-reference uses one of two formats depending on the platform configuration:

| Platform | Format | Example |
|----------|--------|---------|
| Azure DevOps (native) | `WI#<numeric-id>` | `WI#4821` |
| GitHub/ADO Cross-link | `AB#<numeric-id>` | `AB#4821` |

The `WI#` or `AB#` identifier is the ADO work item ID — the number that appears in the work item URL and in the ADO board view. Teams must document which format they use in their repository configuration and use it consistently.

```
│   As a member                                               │
│   I need my enrollment submission validated immediately     │
│   So that I receive clear feedback on any errors before     │
│   the submission is processed                               │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

│                                                             │

│   Scenario: Missing email address is rejected               │
│     Given a member submits an enrollment without an email   │
│           address                                           │
│     When the submission is validated                        │
│     Then the validation result is "rejected"                │
│     And the error code is "EMAIL_REQUIRED"                  │
│                                                             │
│   @FR-ENR-SUB-030                                           │
│   Scenario: Invalid date of birth format is rejected        │
│     Given a member submits an enrollment with date of birth │
│           "13/32/1990"                                      │
│     When the submission is validated                        │
│     Then the validation result is "rejected"                │
│     And the error code is "DOB_INVALID_FORMAT"              │
│                                                             │
│   @FR-ENR-SUB-040                                           │
│   Scenario: Future date of birth is rejected                │
│     Given a member submits an enrollment with date of birth │
│           "2099-01-01"                                      │
│     When the submission is validated                        │
│     Then the validation result is "rejected"                │
│     And the error code is "DOB_FUTURE_DATE"                 │
│                                                             │
│   @FR-ENR-SUB-050                                           │
│   Scenario: Duplicate submission is rejected                │
│     Given a member has an existing active enrollment        │
│     When the member submits a new enrollment with the same  │
│          member ID                                          │
│     Then the validation result is "rejected"                │
│     And the error code is "DUPLICATE_ENROLLMENT"            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Parent:         Feature — Member Enrollment Processing      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Why this is well-formed:**
- Title follows `[Concern] — [Capability]` format
- Story narrative uses domain vocabulary from the glossary
- Five Gherkin scenarios with concrete values — no vague assertions
- Each scenario is independently verifiable
- Tags include `concern:enrollment` and `bdd`
- Parent link to Feature established
page_texts.33:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#example-2-bdd-story--cache-ttl-enforcement]

### Example 2: BDD Story — Cache TTL Enforcement

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Title:          Clock — Cache TTL enforcement               │
│ Work Item Type: User Story                                  │
│ State:          New                                          │
│ Area Path:      EAP\Clock                                   │
│ Iteration Path: EAP\Sprint 15                               │
│ Tags:           concern:clock, bdd, sprint:15               │
│ Priority:       2                                           │
│ Story Points:   3                                           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Description:                                                │
│                                                             │
│   As a system operator                                      │
│   I need cached entries to expire after their configured    │
│   time-to-live                                              │
│   So that stale data is not served beyond the defined       │
│   freshness window                                          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Acceptance Criteria:                                        │
│                                                             │
│   @FR-CLK-TTL-010                                           │
│   Scenario: Entry expires after TTL elapses                 │
│     Given a cache entry with TTL of 300 seconds             │
│     When 301 seconds have elapsed since insertion           │
│     Then the entry is no longer retrievable                 │
│                                                             │
│   @FR-CLK-TTL-020                                           │
│   Scenario: Entry is available before TTL elapses           │
│     Given a cache entry with TTL of 300 seconds             │
│     When 299 seconds have elapsed since insertion           │
│     Then the entry is retrievable with its original value   │
│                                                             │
│   @FR-CLK-TTL-030                                           │
│   Scenario: Zero TTL entry is never cached                  │
│     Given a cache entry with TTL of 0 seconds               │
│     When the entry is inserted                              │
│     Then the entry is not retrievable                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Parent:         Feature — Time-Aware Caching                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#example-3-non-bdd-story--infrastructure]

### Example 3: Non-BDD Story — Infrastructure

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Title:          Infrastructure — S3 audit log bucket        │
│ Work Item Type: User Story                                  │
│ State:          New                                          │
│ Area Path:      EAP\Infrastructure                          │
│ Iteration Path: EAP\Sprint 14                               │
│ Tags:           concern:infrastructure, sprint:14           │
│ Priority:       1                                           │
│ Story Points:   2                                           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Description:                                                │
│                                                             │
│   As a security engineer                                    │
│   I need an S3 bucket provisioned for audit log storage     │
│   So that application audit logs are durably stored in a    │
│   HIPAA-compliant, tamper-evident location                  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Acceptance Criteria:                                        │
│                                                             │
│   1. [ ] Terraform module provisions an S3 bucket with      │
│          versioning enabled and AES-256 server-side          │
│          encryption                                         │
│   2. [ ] Bucket policy restricts access to the application  │
│          IAM role ARN only — no public access               │
│   3. [ ] Object Lock is enabled in compliance mode with a   │
│          365-day retention period                           │
│   4. [ ] terraform plan shows no changes after a second     │
│          apply (idempotent)                                 │
│   5. [ ] Module passes terraform validate and tflint with   │
│          zero errors                                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Parent:         Feature — Audit Log Infrastructure          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Why non-BDD is correct here:** This story provisions infrastructure — it has no behavioral input/output logic. The acceptance criteria are concrete, independently verifiable checklist items rather than Given/When/Then scenarios.
page_texts.35:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#example-4-non-bdd-story--non-functional-requirement]

### Example 4: Non-BDD Story — Non-Functional Requirement

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Title:          Eligibility — API response time SLA         │
│ Work Item Type: User Story                                  │
│ State:          New                                          │
│ Area Path:      EAP\Eligibility                             │
│ Iteration Path: EAP\Backlog                                 │
│ Tags:           concern:eligibility                         │
│ Priority:       2                                           │
│ Story Points:   5                                           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Description:                                                │
│                                                             │
│   As an eligibility worker                                  │
│   I need the eligibility determination API to respond       │
│   within performance targets                                │
│   So that I can process member inquiries without delays     │
│   during peak enrollment periods                            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Acceptance Criteria:                                        │
│                                                             │
│   1. [ ] P50 response time is below 100ms under normal      │
│          load (500 concurrent users)                        │
│   2. [ ] P95 response time is below 200ms under normal      │
│          load (500 concurrent users)                        │
│   3. [ ] P99 response time is below 500ms under peak        │
│          load (2000 concurrent users)                       │
│   4. [ ] Load test results are captured in a report with    │
│          percentile distribution charts                     │
│   5. [ ] No errors (HTTP 5xx) under normal load; error      │
│          rate below 0.1% under peak load                    │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Parent:         Feature — Eligibility API Performance       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Why non-BDD is correct here:** Performance targets are non-functional requirements. They define measurable thresholds, not behavioral input/output scenarios. Gherkin is not the right tool for "P95 latency < 200ms."
page_texts.36:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#example-5-bdd-story--behavioral-non-functional-requirement-session-timeout]

### Example 5: BDD Story — Behavioral Non-Functional Requirement (Session Timeout)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Title:          Session — Idle session invalidation         │
│ Work Item Type: User Story                                  │
│ State:          New                                          │
│ Area Path:      EAP\Session                                 │
│ Iteration Path: EAP\Sprint 16                               │
│ Tags:           concern:session, bdd, sprint:16             │
│ Priority:       1                                           │
│ Story Points:   3                                           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Description:                                                │
│                                                             │
│   As a security engineer                                    │
│   I need idle sessions to be automatically invalidated      │
│   after the configured timeout                              │
│   So that unattended sessions cannot be exploited by        │
│   unauthorized actors                                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Acceptance Criteria:                                        │
│                                                             │
│   @NFR-SES-TO-010                                           │
│   Scenario: Session expires after idle timeout elapses      │
│     Given an authenticated session with idle timeout of     │
│           15 minutes                                        │
│     When 16 minutes elapse with no activity                 │
│     Then the session is invalidated                         │
│     And subsequent requests return HTTP 401                 │
│                                                             │
│   @NFR-SES-TO-020                                           │
│   Scenario: Active session remains valid before timeout     │
│     Given an authenticated session with idle timeout of     │
│           15 minutes                                        │
│     When 14 minutes elapse with no activity                 │
│     Then the session remains valid                          │
│     And subsequent requests are processed normally          │
│                                                             │
│   @NFR-SES-TO-030                                           │
│   Scenario: Activity resets the idle timer                  │
│     Given an authenticated session with idle timeout of     │
│           15 minutes                                        │
│     When 10 minutes elapse and a request is made            │
│     And another 10 minutes elapse after the request         │
│     Then the session remains valid                          │
│                                                             │
│   @NFR-SES-TO-040                                           │
│   Scenario: Expired session cannot be reactivated           │
│     Given an authenticated session that has been            │
│           invalidated due to idle timeout                   │
│     When the user attempts to make a request               │
│     Then the response is HTTP 401                           │
│     And re-authentication is required                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Parent:         Feature — Session Security Controls         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Why BDD is correct here:** Although session timeout is a non-functional security requirement, it describes observable, deterministic behavior — "Given idle time exceeds threshold, When a request arrives, Then 401." This is testable at the unit/integration level with time manipulation. The `@NFR-` tag prefix distinguishes it from functional requirements while following the same Gherkin authoring conventions.

## Part 7: Quality Checklist

Before submitting a User Story, verify every item:
page_texts.38:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#structure]

### Structure

- [ ] Title follows `[Concern] — [Capability summary]` format
- [ ] Description contains a complete As a / I need / So that narrative
- [ ] Acceptance Criteria field is populated (Gherkin for BDD, numbered checklist for non-BDD)
- [ ] Tags include `concern:<name>` matching the concern directory
- [ ] Tags include `bdd` if and only if the acceptance criteria are Gherkin scenarios
- [ ] Parent link to a Feature is set — no orphan stories
page_texts.39:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#content-quality]

### Content Quality

- [ ] Every noun and verb in the story matches the project glossary (`docs/glossary.md`)
- [ ] No implementation details in the story narrative — "what" not "how"
- [ ] All acceptance criteria are independently verifiable — an observer can confirm pass/fail
- [ ] Concrete values everywhere — no "valid input," "correct result," "appropriate level," or "properly configured"
- [ ] No real data — all example values are synthetic
page_texts.40:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#bdd-specific]

### BDD-Specific

- [ ] Gherkin scenarios are pasted verbatim from the `.feature` file — not summarized or paraphrased
- [ ] Each scenario has a unique `@FR-` or `@NFR-` tag following the project's naming convention
- [ ] Scenario count is between 3 and 15 — fewer means the story is too narrow, more means it should be split
- [ ] One `When` step per scenario — multiple `When` steps means multiple behaviors that should be separate scenarios
page_texts.41:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#sizing-and-scope]

### Sizing and Scope

- [ ] Story is estimable — the team can assign story points without further clarification
- [ ] Story is demonstrable — it can be shown at sprint review independently
- [ ] Story does not mix concerns — all scenarios or criteria belong to one concern directory
- [ ] Story does not mix types — behavioral (BDD) and infrastructure (non-BDD) are separate stories

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-007-ado-user-story-authoring-guidance.md#common-mistakes]

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Problem | Fix |
|---------|---------|-----|
| Summarizing Gherkin into bullet points | The acceptance criteria are no longer executable — the engineer must guess what the scenarios said | Paste the full Given/When/Then text verbatim |
| Using "should" in acceptance criteria | "The system should validate" is not verifiable — it leaves room for interpretation | Use definitive language: "the validation result is 'rejected'" |
| Mixing concerns in one story | A story with enrollment validation AND eligibility determination crosses bounded contexts | Split into two stories, one per concern |
| No `concern:` tag | Story cannot be filtered by functional area in ADO queries and dashboards | Add `concern:<name>` matching the concern directory |
| Orphan story (no parent Feature) | Breaks the Epic → Feature → Story hierarchy; story has no traceability to business capability | Create the Feature first, then link the story |
| Writing acceptance criteria in Discussion | Engineers look at the Acceptance Criteria field, not Discussion — criteria in Discussion are invisible during sprint execution | Move criteria to the Acceptance Criteria field |
| Adding implementation notes to acceptance criteria | "Use Redis for caching" or "Call the ValidationService" are implementation decisions, not requirements | Remove implementation details — the acceptance criteria say _what_, the engineer decides _how_ |
| Estimating story points before engineering input | Story points reflect implementation complexity — the PO cannot estimate this alone | Provide the scenario count as a starting estimate; the engineer adjusts at sprint planning |
